# Independent audit: varying bodies with convergent coarse fibers

**Result: PASS.** This audits Section 5 of
`candidate 0639bd50a01557c4`, as read
after its addition of the varying-body statement. The preceding
uniform discrepancy and fixed-body statements have a separate audit.

The hypotheses used here are essential: a common bounded ambient box,
the SAME finite nonempty coarse support P, individual Hausdorff
convergence Q_(l,j) -> Q_j for every j in P, fine-lattice covering
radius tending to zero, and strictly positive limiting full coarse
mass M_*. Ambient Hausdorff convergence alone is not substituted for
the individual fiber hypothesis.

## 1. Measures and closed caps

For a full-dimensional convex limiting fiber Q_j, every interior point
eventually lies in Q_(l,j), and every point outside Q_j eventually lies
outside it. The former follows, for example, from uniform convergence
of support functions and the positive support-distance margin at an
interior point. Its boundary has Lebesgue measure zero. Bounded
convergence gives convergence of indicator functions in L1. If Q_j
has lower dimension, Q_(l,j) lies in a shrinking neighborhood of a
bounded Lebesgue-null set, so its volume tends to zero; the same L1
conclusion holds. There are only finitely many j, proving total
variation convergence of the unnormalized coarse measures.

The sampling discrepancy is uniform in the convex body within the
fixed box and uniform in the closed cap. Adding it to the L1 error,
and using M_*>0 for normalization, proves uniform normalized closed-cap
discrepancy. Coarse fibers of zero limiting or prelimit volume are
included. No sampled boundary mass is discarded and no total-variation
convergence of the singular fine measures to the coarse measure is
asserted.

## 2. Compatibility and exact limiting fibers

For every convex representation j=sum t_i j_i in P, approximating
chosen points of Q_(j_i) by points of Q_(l,j_i) and using convexity of
K_l gives sum t_i Q_(j_i) subset Q_j. Conversely each Q_j is among the
generators of the lifted convex hull D. These two inclusions give
exact equality between D's fiber at j and Q_j.

The common support P is lattice-convex: every integer point of conv(P)
is a base in every K_l, hence is in P. The projection of D is conv(P),
so it has no additional integer fibers. This argument does not assume
full affine rank of P or positive volume of every Q_j.

## 3. The two depth inequalities

For the upper limit, any approximate maximizing sequence has a
subsequence with fixed coarse base and convergent continuous
coordinate. Individual fiber Hausdorff convergence places the limit
in Q_j. The depth of nu_* is Lipschitz in ALL continuous coordinates
at any fixed coarse base, including bases with zero own volume:
only positive-volume fibers contribute to the measure; their slab
losses have a common section bound, and pure coarse-base halfspaces
do not change at all. Uniform cap discrepancy therefore proves the
upper bound without assuming that the limiting cap infimum is
attained or that the own fiber has positive volume.

For the lower limit, a positive-depth point has base in the convex
hull of the positive-volume coarse bases, by strict separation.
Compatibility then makes its own fiber full dimensional. Move the
point a little into that fiber. A fixed ball about this interior point
eventually lies in Q_(l,j), by its actual Hausdorff convergence to a
full-dimensional fiber. Rounding the fine base coordinates moves the
point by a quantity tending to zero, and therefore remains feasible.
The Lipschitz estimate and uniform cap discrepancy recover the depth.
There is a positive-depth coarse point by ordinary Grünbaum in any
positive-volume fiber, so this approximation reaches the positive
supremum. This also covers nonattainment of the supremum.

## 4. Full-dimensional ambient realization

If aff(P)=R^k, a positive full coarse fiber together with points above
affinely spanning bases gives a full-dimensional hull D. If aff(P)
is proper, compactness and lattice-convexity give a strictly positive
distance from conv(P) to Z^k minus P. The selected neighborhood can be
taken as conv(P) plus an open Euclidean ball, a convex set. Choose a
small ambient ball with base projection in that neighborhood and
strictly on one side of an affine hyperplane containing aff(P).

The convex hull with D stays in the chosen base neighborhood and
therefore adds no integer bases. At any base j in P, the separating
affine functional is zero, whereas it is strictly positive throughout
the added ball's projection. A convex representation above j thus
cannot use a positive weight from that ball. This proves exact
preservation of every Q_j, including lower-dimensional ones, while
the added ambient ball supplies full dimension. For k=0, M_*>0
already supplies full dimension.

No correction is needed. The result proves exact maximal-depth
convergence under the stated fiberwise hypotheses; it supplies neither
a decomposition of arbitrary moving lattices nor a treatment of a
vanishing limiting coarse mass.
